feedback: Written before this geometry has raced. Evidence from iteration 0: all 60 baseline trials went off track after one line-loss event each, with max_error about 0.06 to 0.069 and low steering_oscillation (0.07 to 0.15), so the failure was early drift rather than jitter. What I had to do: I kept the sensor-x-proportional weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] because the baseline signal was smooth across the span, I lowered base_speed to 1.6 to limit overshoot from the lookahead change, and I raised kd slightly to 0.15 to damp the faster response of the closer, larger-footprint sensors. The y = 0.03 row and the 16 mm footprint are untested on the controller side. Next race, if line_loss_events fall but max_error stays near 0.06 on bends, widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.06 with 5 sensors, which tests whether more span is needed for sharper curves. If steering_oscillation rises above the baseline range (about 0.15), move the row back to y = 0.02 and keep the 16 mm footprint, since the closer row adds response that the controller may not damp. If the robot completes no track but stays on the line and progress stalls, keep the geometry and test a wider track of 0.12 m, since the narrower track may now be too sharp at this speed.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events fall but max_error stays near 0.06 on bends, widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.06 (keep 5 sensors, keep y = 0.03), because the baseline showed max_error at the 0.06 limit with the ±0.04 span.
If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15 with the new row, move the sensor row to y = 0.02 and keep sensor_size 0.016, since the closer row raises response that the 0.03 row may overshoot.

If the robot stays on the line but progress stalls before the course end, try wheel_track 0.12 m, because the 0.10 m track may now be too sharp at this speed; the baseline 0.12 m track had no stall evidence.
